# Purpose and scope

Manifold is for people and teams who design, explain, or improve systems. It gives them shared definitions and a way to connect needs and requirements to how a system is organized and how it works. These connections help expose unclear expectations, missing pieces, and solutions that do not address the need they were meant to serve.

This introduction was [accepted on 2026-09-27](../../notes/decisions/manifold-introduction.md). The supporting definitions retain their own standing, and the unresolved questions below remain unresolved.

## Scope and rationale

Owner direction: develop a standard useful to an individual and a business, reflecting the time, uncertainty and choices involved in operating either. The working title includes execution because the owner wants to understand how processes are implemented and operated, as well as how the arrangement fits together.

The standard must help reveal unclear purpose, inspiration without articulated purpose, needs or wants with missing requirements, tool choices made before needs and requirements, unclear responsibility, and designs with unexplained contribution to needs or high-level requirements.

In scope: purpose; needs and requirements; process, structure and systems; composition and interaction; responsibilities and authority; intended contribution; relevant instances, events and history; meaning and evidence limits of assessment results; durable representation and review questions.

Detailed system development and verification methods remain a separate discussion. The title's execution dimension does not silently expand this boundary. The semantics and results of evaluation belong here because usefulness cannot be assessed from intended design alone. See the [scope decision](../../notes/decisions/system-verification-boundary.md).

The owner's initial assumption was that if systems do what they are required to do, the needs put forward will be met. The [accepted adequacy decision](../../notes/decisions/requirements-to-needs-adequacy.md) qualifies that inference: explain why the requirements cover the need in the stated circumstances and establish that the required combination is satisfied. Incomplete requirements can be met while the need remains unmet. Unclear meanings are raised, with handling left to the environment and dependent conclusions remaining unknown until clarified. The [rule and three examples](../ontology/concepts/requirement.md#from-requirement-fulfillment-to-need-fulfillment) resolve F2/EOM-02 at this scope.

Exploration, learning, enjoyment and curiosity may themselves be legitimate purposes. Personal use must allow qualitative judgment and uncertainty without fabricated numeric precision. Costs, competing needs and adverse effects must be considered; more output alone may not mean greater usefulness.

Pi learning-to-writing motivates examples, but its tools, implementation choices and runtime state are not rules of this standard. See [the example](../../../source-locators.md#source-1bbc5bd383de5da4).
